en: And I could look into your dreamy eyes for hours, Ken-kun!
Let's do it, then!
Oh, come on. You're making me blush.
(They're in good spirits.)
Your makeup looks amazing today, Mi-tan!
Thanks! I copied it off this idol I saw on TV, Haruka Sawamura!
I see. But you're much cuter than Haruka Sawamura, Mi-tan!
No way! You're just saying that.
No, I mean it! You're just as pretty as any of those idols, Mi-tan!
Hey, driver. My girl's way cuter than Haruka Sawamura, right?
Of course, your girlfriend is cuter.
See!? The driver agrees with me! You could even be on TV if you wanted, Mi-tan!
Yay! Maybe I'll start looking for an agency.
Hehe, you'd be a star in no time!
(At least they're happy.)
No, I think Haruka Sawamura is cuter.
What!? Have you got something wrong with your eyes? My Mi-tan is the prettiest girl in the world!
I don't agree.
Are you dissing my girl, driver?
Tch. I hate this guy!
Don't cry, Mi-tan!
Even if the world's against you, I'll always have your back!
Oh, Ken-kun...
Mi-tan...
I love you, Ken-kun!
A pretty face isn't everything, you know.
Huh? What's that supposed to mean?

en: So you focus on the body more, do you?
Now that I think about it, I did get the feeling he was checking out my boobs and butt in the mirror.
Driver! I know Mi-tan is a perfect ten, but you shouldn't leer at her like that!
I wasn't.
Ugh. Boys are always staring at me like I'm a piece of meat.
It can't be helped, Mi-tan. You're just too damn attractive!
But you'll always be my one and only, Ken-kun!
I love you, Mi-tan!
Say, Mi-tan.
Yes, Ken-kun?
Did you talk to your dad about us getting married?
Oh. Well, about that...
Dad says he's completely against me marrying a guy who doesn't have a job.
Huh!? But what does that matter!? Can't he see how much we love each other!?
All we need is love, right? Work has nothing to do with it!
Yeah! I think so, too!
Let's run away together in this taxi, Mi-tan!
Yeah! Let's elope, Ken-kun!
Driver, just take us someplace far away!
I'm afraid I can't do that.
Huh? Why not!?
Do you have money on you for a trip like that?
Uh, how much do you have, Mi-tan?
Me!? I don't have anything on me today! Don't you have any cash, Ken-kun?
I've got around 3,000 yen.
That won't even get us out of Fukuoka...
I guess we need money if we want to run off and get married, huh? I'd better look for a job.
I'm sure you can get one easily, Ken-kun!
Yeah! Once I have a job, your dad might even warm up to the idea of us getting married!
That's right! That'd be perfect!
We won't be going anywhere today, driver.
(They're finally coming down to earth.)
All right! Thanks, driver!
You're too kind!
Yeah! He was moved by the depth of our love!
I guess even without money, as long as you have love you can get by!
Hold on. You mean you don't have any money?
Of course not. I don't have a job, after all.
And what about the fare for this trip?
I thought you were going to take us for free?
This is my job. I can't do that.
Oh, what a stingy man!
Grownups think about nothing but cash!
(Somehow I ended up getting yelled at.)
Thank you! Here's the fare. I wish I could give you a tip, but 3,000 yen is all I have.
I hope you find the same happiness we have soon!
See you!
(Well, at least they're in a good mood.)
Thank you! Here's the fare.
I know you're single, but you really need to control that jealous streak. This ride was really kind of awkward.
Let's get out of here, Mi-tan.
(Love birds are hard to please, apparently.)
Heheh. <Color:22>Suzukake Lane<Color:Default>, please.
Man, I'm stuffed. Couldn't eat another bite.
What did you have?
Foie gras. Then caviar, and truffles.
(He must be a lot richer than he looks.)
How are you able to afford stuff like that?
That's a nasty thing to say, driver. Are you insinuating I look poor?
Oh, no. I wouldn't do that.
If you're smart, you don't need money to get what you want. Hehehe.
(So he doesn't have any money? How does he afford gourmet food like that, then?)
I'm very jealous.
Heheheh. It all comes down to legwork in the end. I've been training.
(Legwork?)
That's pretty gourmet stuff. Did you dine and dash or something?
Hey, now! You shouldn't go around accusing people of things!
(I guess he didn't appreciate the joke. Why that reaction, though?)
Heheh. I did good, even if I do say so myself.
(What a strange guy. He's got me curious.)
What do you do for a living?
Oh, I don't work.
But how do you put food on the table?
Heheh. It's pretty narrow-minded to assume you need a job to eat, driver.
(Hmm. He doesn't look like he's from a rich family.)
What sort of sports do you like?
I run marathons. I did some pretty major ones years back. Heheh.
(Sounds like he's fast on his feet.)
Do you have any special talents?
I know this town real well. I've got a map of every nook and cranny in my head.
Wow. That's amazing.
Heheh. Yeah.
(I'm feeling uneasy for some reason.)
Here we are. The fare comes to⑬
Heheh. I'll show you how I'm able to eat all that gourmet stuff, driver.
Step one... Hey, look over there!
(Hey! No free ride for him if I can help it!)
How the hell did you catch up to me? No regular taxi driver could do that!
Hey, what's going on over there!?
Hm? You're that Okada guy! There's a warrant out for you!
He's been scamming local restaurants for a while now.
Thought you could get away without paying your fare, huh? Surely you can afford a taxi ride with all those meals you've been skipping out on! Now pay up, you scoundrel!
All right, all right! Grr...
Now, you're coming with me.
I'll outrun you next time, driver. You just wait.
Hmph. We'll see.
Thanks for assisting with the arrest. Bye!
(Damn, he got away. Now I'm out the taxi fare.)
(I'll have to keep an eye on any other suspicious passengers I pick up.)
(He doesn't seem like a typical office worker.)
Hi! Can you give me a ride?
Where are you headed?
Nowhere in particular right now. Can I get you to just drive for a while?
Okay. How long are we talking?
Well, that depends on the conversation.
(Hm. What a strange passenger.)
Taxi drivers meet all sorts of people, right?
Then you're probably a good judge of people. See if you can guess my job.
Are you a breeder?
Huh? A breeder?
Someone who breeds dogs or other animals.
Yeah, I know it is. But why did you peg me for one?
Just a wild guess.
Haha! That's interesting! I always ask the people I interview the same question, but I've never heard that answer before.
People you interview?
Oh, sorry for not introducing myself. I'm a freelance writer. The name's Muranaka.
Ah. A freelance writer.
Oh, and I own three dogs. So you weren't necessarily too far off!
Are you a part-timer?
What? A part-timer?
Whoa. What makes you say that? It's not exactly the most prestigious thing I've been called.
Sorry. You just looked the type that doesn't take their job very seriously.
Wow. And there's the double punch. Well, I do try not to be too formal with my work.
It can put the interview subjects on edge, so I opt for a more casual approach.
Interview?
Well, I guess a lot of us freelance writers work part-time, so you weren't too far off the mark.
Are you a freelance writer?
Wow! You got it in one guess! You're pretty good at sizing people up, all right! This should make for an interesting interview.
Oh, sorry for not introducing myself. The name's Muranaka. And I'm a freelance writer, just like you said.
Why are you interviewing taxi drivers?
I believe variety is the spice of life. I meet all sorts of people in my job, but I figured taxi drivers would have even more perspective.
So I've been interviewing cabbies all over the country to hear their stories. I'm putting together an article on it.
I see. How are the interviews going?
Well, I've interviewed a few drivers already, but all they want to do is boast about the big tips they got back during the bubble economy.
Do you have any stories that stand out in particular? It can be anything.
(Something that stands out, huh?)
Well, not long after I started this job, I was given a 50,000 yen tip.
Okay, here we go again. Let me guess, this was back during the bubble economy.
No, it was six months ago.
Only recently? Wait, you mean you've only just started this job? Aren't you a little old to be starting a whole new career like that?
Perhaps.
Wow! What triggered the change? To be honest, I'm more interested in that than the 50,000 yen.
(I don't get these writer types.)
I'd rather not dig up the past.
Oh, I see. That's a shame.
But it's my policy to not press too hard when someone doesn't want to talk about something. I'll leave it at that.
I guess the first day I did this job is what sticks out in my memory.
I see. Memories of your first day as a driver.
I'm not from around here, so I wasn't confident I could navigate properly. It was nerve-wracking not knowing if I'd reach the destination.
Anyway, I finally got my first passenger.
It turned out to be an elementary school boy who'd never ridden in a taxi before.
He brought a map showing the way to his grandmother's house, which helped me a lot.
I see. So it was a first for both of you. He must have been nervous.
Yes. But after he had paid and got out, he looked so much more grown up to me than when he first got in.
It motivated me to knuckle down and be brave, just like that little kid.
(Huh? Maybe he's not that interested.)
That's a great story, driver! I'd love to write about it in my article!
You're welcome to.
(I'm glad I could give him some good material.)
Nothing really stands out to me.
Oh, I see. But surely there's something you can tell me about?
No, nothing really comes to mind.
Okay. I just thought a driver like you might have a unique perspective on things. Never mind.
(I should have given it a bit more thought.)
I don't suppose you have any inside stories on the taxi industry, do you?
Things that are ordinary for people in your line of work, but not well known by others.
(Let me see...)
You know the light on the roof of taxis?
Yes. The one with the company name on it, right?
They usually aren't switched on unless the taxi is empty, but you can make them blink red to warn others in an emergency.
Wow, really!? I never knew that! Where is the switch that makes them blink?
I'm afraid I can't tell you that. It's somewhere you can push without alerting the passenger.
Oh, now I'm curious. But I think I could still use this in my article!
Do you know what happens to the meter when you reverse in a taxi?
No, I don't! What does it do? Does the meter go down or something?
No, that wouldn't make sense. When you shift into reverse the meter treats it the same as when you are stopped.
So if you went the whole way in reverse, you could go anywhere for free!?
Well, there aren't any roads you could do that on. And when you're stopped, the meter still goes up based on time.
Oh, so it'll still cost you. Hmm, I think I could turn that into something for my article, though. Thanks!
I could tell you about taxi jargon. That said, I haven't been doing this long, so these are just things I've heard from my colleagues.
A flag is someone who flags you down on the street.
A bingo is someone who flags you down when you already have a passenger.
Drivers sometimes call in bingos so another taxi can come and pick them up.
Are you not that interested in this?
No, it's interesting, for sure.
But because these aren't terms you use yourself, I can't figure out an angle for my article.
(I guess I should have spoken from experience.)
Thank you so much for a fruitful ride. I have plenty of material for my article now!
Here's the fare, and a tip for your help!
I'll do my best to write a great article! Good luck with the job!
Thank you for the ride! I think I have plenty of material for my article! Here's the fare.
Hmm. I think I'll need to take a few more rides before I have enough material. Here's the fare.
Bye.
(Maybe I should have provided more useful information.)
It's the client from the highway rest stop. Just like before, he was very polite.
(Cool Yoshimi of the Devil Killers again.)
I'm done with this. I hate studying!
If you're going to have that attitude, then I hate teaching you!
Then let me be already! It's not like I'm gonna become a genius overnight!
You don't have a hope of getting your Class 2 license with that kind of talk!
Like I said⑬
